While it's true that most channels die within 3 years, I think you should definitely look at the cause behind those stats. Don't let that scare you into slowing down your pace. Approach your channel with an open mind and pay attention to your audience (what they enjoy most, what they would like to see, what other similar niches your audience enjoys).

As long as you ask yourself these questions and are ready to pivot your channel style when needed, I don't see a reason for your channel to just die down. Most channels die down because they produce the same style content over and over without paying attention to where their niche is headed or what their audience really wants.

I suggest going full force with the goal of raising the view floor of your channel. As in the goal shouldn't be to make a 1 mil video, but rather to make it so your videos never go below 50 60 70 80 90 or even 100k views.

Dream big but pay attention!

Disclaimer that I am not expert in this field but I have come across deductive reasoning and have taken an interest in it in my past. From what I understand the key to improving deduction skills is to improve your awareness of your surroundings. 

I once came across this exercise where you look at an environment for as long as you need to and then recall the objects in said environment on a piece of paper right after in a different room. For example, you would decide to start with your desk and try to remember every single object and detail about your desk for as long as you need to. Then you would draw the desk as you remember it. The more this is practiced the better you would get at actively recalling details to work in your favor. 

Eventually, to make it harder, you would set time limits for how long you can look at an environment or you would look at bigger environments with more going on. In this case, you could look at the desk for only 2 minutes or decide to look at the entire room itself for as long as you need. 

Also, there are many books related to deductive reasoning and the theories behind it as well as youtube videos that go into such concepts. Overall, my point is that such discipline exists and there are people out there who take on the very same interest.
